blocks.text:
Start the morning with an optional workout on the upper deck as the yacht approaches Punta Espinoza on Fernandina Island. This area lies within an immense lava flow formed by one of the many eruptions of La Cumbre, one of the world's most active volcanoes.

Fernandina is renowned for its large colonies of marine iguanas, flightless cormorants, Galápagos penguins, hawks, lizards and snakes. Spend the morning exploring ashore, with an opportunity to snorkel.

Back on board, enjoy lunch followed by a talk on the geology of the Galápagos Islands given by one of the expert guides.

The yacht then crosses the Bolívar Channel and returns to Isabela Island. The next stop is Tagus Cove, a former anchorage for pirates and whalers. Set beside a volcanic crater, this bay is sometimes referred to as the 'land of the marine iguana'.

On a hike, see Darwin Lake, a saltwater lake within a tuff cone. Alternatively, choose one of the yacht's eight two-person kayaks, go snorkelling, paddle through the bay or explore it aboard the yacht's elegant black boats.

Return to the yacht around sunset. After dinner, relax on deck or chat with the captain. On the way to the next anchorage, the yacht crosses the Equator twice as it rounds the north of Isabela.
